extracted.intended_audience: patent proprietors, potential opponents, defendants in infringement actions, and patent attorneys considering or involved in European Patent Office opposition and appeal proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural standards for initiating, conducting and appealing oppositions to European patents before the EPO, including grounds, timing, evidence and amendment rules. Aimed at parties (and their representatives) deciding strategy and complying with procedural requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit to file an opposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Opposition proceedings may be initiated against a European patent within nine months after publication of the mention of its grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The nine-month period is non-extendible; although an opposition may be filed immediately after grant, the Opposition Division normally starts examination only after expiration of the nine-month opposition period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file an opposition
rubrics_metrics.description: An opposition may be filed by any natural or legal person; no legal interest of the opponent has to be proven; a 'straw man' (a person with no real interest acting for an unknown third person) may be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oppositions are typically filed in reaction to national infringement actions or as a precautionary means against competitors' patents because costs are relatively low.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admissible grounds for revocation (grounds of opposition)
rubrics_metrics.description: A European patent may only be opposed on the grounds that: (1) the subject-matter of one or more claims is not patentable (in particular not new or not inventive); (2) the patent does not disclose the invention sufficiently clearly and completely for it to be carried out by a person skilled in the art; (3) the subject-matter of the patent extends beyond the content of the application as filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other grounds of opposition are not admissible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inadmissible grounds of opposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Opposition may not be based on the grounds that the wording of the claims lacks clarity, or that the claimed invention was 'stolen' from the opponent or a third party by the patent proprietor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition Division composition and allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: An Opposition Division generally consists of three technically qualified members; it may be enlarged by a legal member if complex legal questions are to be decided, and a legal member is generally called upon for taking evidence on alleged prior public use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The competent Opposition Division is determined according to the technical field of the case; Divisions sit in Munich, Berlin or The Hague.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of examination by the Opposition Division
rubrics_metrics.description: The Opposition Division considers legal questions and evaluates the facts on its own motion (ex officio) but is bound to the extent to which the patent has been opposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the opposition attacks only certain independent claims, other independent claims of the granted patent are not to be examined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence submission timing and admissibility (first instance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Opponents should cite all known evidence and, in particular, all known prior art against the patent before the expiry of the opposition period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After expiration of the opposition period, admission of new facts and evidence is subject to the discretion of the Opposition Division, primarily exercised on the basis of relevance, and exercised restrictively after the time limit set in the summons to oral proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure of written exchange and oral proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: A written exchange of briefs takes place after filing; if requested by at least one party, the Opposition Division summons the parties to oral proceedings. The summons includes a non-binding preliminary opinion of the Opposition Division.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preliminary opinion indicates issues considered relevant or gives a preliminary assessment; oral proceedings are typically requested and form an important stage of examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment rules for the patent proprietor
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent proprietor may defend the opposed patent as granted or in a limited version; amendments may be chosen from the whole content of the original patent application's disclosure as long as the scope of protection is not extended beyond the granted patent's scope of protection; amendments need to be occasioned by a ground of opposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opposition proceedings must not be used to reformulate claims or description for clarity/cosmetic reasons or to adapt to competitors' embodiments. Amendments must be supported by the original disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Main and auxiliary requests and limits on new requests
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent proprietor may defend the patent in different versions via a main request and one or more auxiliary requests; an auxiliary request is considered only if the main or higher-ranking auxiliary request fails to meet EPC requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission of new requests is procedurally limited. Requests submitted in oral proceedings are, as a rule, not admitted unless they can be readily discussed by the panel and the opponent or are a reaction to a new objection made in the oral proceedings. Primarily only small editorial amendments may be made during oral proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal time limits and content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Any party adversely affected by the Opposition Division decision may appeal within two months after receipt of the decision; the appeal must be reasoned within another non-extendible two-month period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: According to the Rules of Procedure of the Boards of Appeal, the statement of grounds of appeal shall contain the appellant’s complete case, including all legal and technical arguments as well as any modified main and auxiliary requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boards of Appeal composition and procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal is handled by a competent Technical Board of Appeal (there are 28 Technical Boards + one Legal Board). A Technical Board of Appeal generally sits as two technical members and one legal member; under certain circumstances composition may include more members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At the end of oral proceedings the Board issues its decision. Appeals typically take another two to two and a half years, varying by technical field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admission of new facts, evidence or requests in appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: In appeal proceedings, the Boards of Appeal exercise discretion to admit new facts, evidence or requests considering relevance, complexity, state of the proceedings and procedural economy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions which could have been made or were rejected in first instance may be rejected; late submissions requiring canceling or postponement of oral proceedings will, as a rule, not be admitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural governance and language rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Opposition proceedings are governed by the EPC, Implementing Regulations and the Guidelines (Part D); the appeal follows the Rules of Procedure of the Boards of Appeal. Parties may use any of the three official EPO languages (English, German, French). Oral proceedings are held in the language of proceedings, communications and final decisions are issued in the language of proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each party may express itself in any of the three official languages and interpretation between them is provided on prior request at no extra cost; Boards of Appeal are not bound to apply the Guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of experts
rubrics_metrics.description: The law allows appointment of an expert, but taking of evidence by appointing a technical expert is rarely ordered ex officio. Parties may present private experts who may submit written opinions and, upon prior notice to the EPO, appear at oral proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation before the EPO in opposition proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: A party may be represented by a professional representative admitted to practice before the EPO, in particular by a European Patent Attorney.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opposition proceedings are regularly handled by European Patent Attorneys who may support attorneys-at-law in national infringement proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of withdrawal of opposition or appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: An opposition may be withdrawn at any time by the opponent, but such withdrawal does not necessarily terminate the opposition proceedings; the Opposition Division may continue proceedings on its own motion and issue a decision within the framework of the original opposition. Withdrawal of the (only) appeal will terminate the second instance opposition appeal proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This particularity must be considered in settlement considerations, since an opposed patent may still be revoked although the opponent has withdrawn and no longer participates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intervention by defendant in parallel national infringement proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: A defendant in patent infringement proceedings may intervene in pending opposition proceedings within three months from the institution of infringement proceedings; the defendant must accept the opposition proceedings in their current stage but may introduce new grounds of opposition and submit new facts and evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic interaction with national invalidity proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: If no opposition is pending, a defendant must consider whether to initiate an opposition within the nine-month period or start national invalidity proceedings against the national part of the patent being enforced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some national courts (e.g., German Federal Patent Court) may apply a higher inventive-step hurdle than the EPO. An action for revocation in Germany is only possible if no opposition is pending at the EPO, so late-filed oppositions can block national nullity suits until final EPO decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs allocation and typical fees
rubrics_metrics.description: In European opposition proceedings, each party generally bears its own costs, including official fees for filing opposition or appeal. An apportionment of costs may exceptionally be ordered, particularly in cases of abuse of procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical attorneys' fees range from EUR 15,000 to EUR 50,000 for each instance depending on complexity; travel expenses, translations, private experts and official fees are additional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-validation and translation costs for maintained-in-amended patents
rubrics_metrics.description: If a European patent has been maintained in amended form, it must be re-validated in all designated states, requiring submission of a translation of the granted patent in which it was initially validated to continue protection in those states.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This leads to further costs beyond opposition/appeal fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retroactive effect of opposition decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: A decision in opposition proceedings is retro-actively effective in all states where the opposed patent is valid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By contrast, national patent invalidity proceedings after the opposition period may lead to differing results between countries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceleration and stays in national courts
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may request acceleration of EPO opposition and appeal proceedings. In Germany, patent infringement proceedings may be stayed at the request of the defendant if the infringement court considers it very likely that the patent will be revoked in the opposition proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision on a stay is discretionary for the infringement court and has no binding or prejudicial effect on the EPO opposition decision.
